channel.title: The Catholic Register - Article Feed
channel.description: Latest articles from The Catholic Register (catholicregister.org)

item.title: Sisters Poor of Jesus open Toronto mission
item.description: The Sisters Poor of Jesus Christ have officially opened the order's new mission house in Toronto on Feb. 1. The new mission marks the second Canadian house of the community, a Catholic institute initially founded in 2001 in Brazil.

item.title: Something's cooking at Mississauga high school
item.description: In a first for Canada, Puratos is bringing professional-level baking education to high school students with the opening of a dedicated bakery school at Mississauga, Ont.'s Father Michael Goetz Secondary School.

item.title: Prayer continues at Holy Sepulchre amid 'time of trial,' restricted access
item.description: The Church of the Holy Sepulchre remains a place of continuous prayer despite restricted access to the faithful, according to a statement released March 21 by the Custody of the Holy Land.

item.title: Pope Leo: Death and pain caused by wars a scandal for entire human family
item.description: As the U.S. and Israel-Iran war enters its fourth week, Pope Leo XIV appealed during his Sunday Angelus prayer March 22: "Persevere in prayer, so that hostilities may cease and paths of peace may finally open up."

item.title: Nova Scotia hospital losing faith identity
item.description: After 120 years as Nova Scotia’s only Catholic hospital, St. Martha’s Regional Hospital in Antigonish will no longer carry its distinctive faith-based identity post-Sept. 30.

item.title: Report shows Cardinal Wojtyla's actions were 'exemplary' in abuse cases, refuting previous claims
item.description: In 2023, following a major television documentary claiming that St. John Paul II had covered up clerical sexual abuse when he was leading the Archdiocese of Kraków, Polish experts rejected the claim and urged that archdiocesan records be opened to allow the full context.

item.title: New hope dawns for pro-life advocates
item.description: March has gifted Canadian culture of life advocates with hope in the form of the Archdiocese of Toronto’s Help Not Harm campaign and the Alberta government’s sweeping euthanasia reform bill.

item.title: Jerusalem patriarchate cancels Palm Sunday procession, postpones chrism Mass amid war
item.description: The Latin Patriarchate of Jerusalem said wartime restrictions have forced the cancellation or postponement of key Holy Week observances, urging the faithful to remain united in prayer despite the inability to gather for traditional celebrations.

item.title: U.S. bishops seek probe of Indian boarding school legacy
item.description: Chairmen of several U.S. Conference of Catholic Bishops committees wrote in a letter to key House lawmakers that they support a bill that would establish an effort to investigate and document the histories and practices of Indian boarding schools, and their long-term effects on Native American peoples.

item.title: New digital bill enshrines same liberty issues
item.description: The 11 months since the 2025 federal election have seen the Liberals introduce several bills with significant digital policy implications: Bill C-2, Bill C-8 and, most recently, Bill C-22, tabled on March 12.
